metaTitle: Mercedes-Benz High-Mileage Engine Rebuild | Mercedes Garage
metaDescription: Specialist high-mileage engine rebuild for Mercedes-Benz. Full disassembly, machining, and replacement of all wear-prone parts to restore your engine's performance and longevity.
lede: Dedicated rebuild service for engines that have covered substantial miles. We carry out a comprehensive strip-down, precision machining, and full parts replacement to bring your Mercedes engine back to its best.

sections.heading: What Makes a High-Mileage Rebuild Different

blocks.html: Engines with high mileage (typically 100,000+ miles) have experienced cumulative wear across multiple systems. A standard rebuild may not be sufficient; a high-mileage rebuild requires a more thorough approach.

items: **More comprehensive parts replacement** — components that are still serviceable in a lower-mileage engine are often at end-of-life here and must be renewed.
**Stricter inspection criteria** — all parts are checked against tighter tolerances because wear is more distributed and hidden damage is more likely.
**Higher machining demand** — cylinder bores, crankshaft journals, and deck surfaces are more likely to be out of specification and require machining to restore geometry.

**Ancillary renewal** — oil pumps, water pumps, and timing components are often replaced as a matter of course, even if they appear functional, because their service life is typically aligned with the engine's major overhaul interval.

blocks.html: We treat every high-mileage engine on its own merits, but our baseline standard is significantly more rigorous than a routine rebuild.

paras: **Our high-mileage rebuilds start from the same base pricing as our standard rebuilds**, but additional machining and parts replacement may increase the final cost. We quote after a full inspection.

steps.title: Full Disassembly & Cleaning
steps.body: The engine is stripped to its bare components. All parts are thoroughly cleaned to allow accurate inspection.

steps.title: Detailed Measurement
steps.body: Critical dimensions — cylinder bores, crankshaft journals, camshaft bearing surfaces — are measured against OE wear limits.

steps.title: Machining & Restoration
steps.body: Bores are honed or bored, crankshafts are ground (if needed), and decks are skimmed to restore flatness.

steps.title: Replacement of All Wear-Prone Parts
steps.body: We install new bearings, pistons, rings, seals, gaskets, timing components, oil pump, and water pump as standard.

steps.title: Reassembly & Testing
steps.body: Precision assembly with new torque-to-yield fasteners, followed by a full test run to confirm oil pressure and compression.

steps.title: Refit & Road Test
steps.body: The engine is refitted, fluids filled, and the vehicle is road-tested to ensure everything performs as expected.

items.q: What qualifies as "high-mileage" for a Mercedes engine?
items.a: We typically consider engines with 100,000+ miles as high-mileage, but the decision also depends on maintenance history, engine type, and usage. We assess each engine individually.

items.q: How does a high-mileage rebuild differ from a standard rebuild?
items.a: It involves more extensive parts replacement (including ancillaries like oil pumps), stricter inspection criteria, and higher likelihood of machining (cylinder bores, crankshaft journals).

items.q: Will my high-mileage engine be as good as new after rebuild?
items.a: With proper machining, new OEM parts, and careful assembly, a high-mileage engine can perform and last as well as a new engine, provided the block is in good condition.

items.q: How long does a high-mileage rebuild take?
items.a: Typically 3-5 working days from arrival at our workshop, though additional machining or parts lead times may extend this slightly.

items.q: What warranty do you offer on high-mileage rebuilds?
items.a: We provide a 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty on all rebuilds, covering parts and labour.
